TESTIMONY OF MATT DUNLAP, CIA
STATE AUDITOR IN SUPPORT
LD 1052 RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution ofMaine to Establish
the StateAuditor as a Constitutional Ojficer

Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on State and Local Government; my name is Matt Dunlap of Old Town, and I have
the honor of serving as Maine's state auditor.

I would like `to thank Rep. Salisbury for sponsoring this important legislation. If approved, first

in this committee, the full Legislature, and finally by the voters, this legislation would establish in bedrock the independenceof the Office of the State Auditor. The nature of the work and the

position of the State Auditor has chang

since the Legislature first established a three-

person audit committee in the 1870's, followed by the creation of the State Auditor in 1907, and

its current disposition in the l93O's.

However, while everything seems to hum along nicely, it is a statutory office. There have been
bills contemplated in the pass to eliminate the office and farm out the work on a contract basis; that has not been pursued, simply because it is not cost-effective. There is, however, the risk that the office could be simply written out of the budget or a threat of such be leveraged to influence the work of the oflice, which would be much to the detriment of the public trust.

We have amended the Constitution something like 177 times, and have in turns created and
eliminated the State Land Agent, taken the Attorney General from a cabinet appointment to a constitutional office, and converted the Adjutant General from a constitutional office to an appointment of the Governor; so such actions are not without either precedent or value.

I am happy to answer any questions now or at the work session at the pleasure of the Chair.

Testimony ofRepresentative Suzanne Salisbury presenting
LD 1052, Resolution, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution
of Maine to Establish the State Auditor as a Constitutional Officer
Before the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government
Senator Baldacci, and esteemed colleagues on the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local
Government, I am Sue Salisbury and I represent House District 128, which includes part of
Westbrook. I am here today to present LD 1052, Resolve, Proposing an Amendment to the
Constitution of Maine to Establish the State Auditor as a Constitutional Officer.
Today, this committee will be hearing or has already heard five bills related to the State Auditor position. Some of these are perennial bills heard every session and, as you will hear, the topic of how these roles are chosen is, at times, contentious. The Attorney General, Secretary of State,
State Treasurer and State Auditor are critical to the smooth operations of the Legislature and the
'
entire state of Maine.
This bill proposes amending Maine's Constitution by adding the State Auditor's role as a constitutional officer. The auditor would be chosen quadrennially by a joint ballot of the senators and representatives in the convention.
I have submitted this bill on behalf of Maine's State Auditor, Matt Dunlap, and would refer any
questions to him.
Thank you for your consideration.

House District 128: Part of Westbrook
